accuracy.evidence: Matches the national curriculum for England: Years 3 and 4 organise paragraphs around a theme and use headings and sub-headings in non-narrative material; the grammar appendix introduces paragraphs to group related material. Animal facts were checked: red fox cubs are born in spring in a den called an earth, owls have 14 neck vertebrae to our 7, a pipistrelle eats thousands of midges a night (Bat Conservation Trust), bats are the only mammals capable of true flight.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real errors: a paragraph has a fixed length (locked prediction, the after-3 break gets 'both about food', challenge 'three', m7), one long block (challenge 'one'), off-theme sentences (grouping step, m3), a sentence or the topic name used as a sub-heading (bat cards, m1, challenge 'sentence' and 'title'), a new speaker kept in the old paragraph (TiPToP prediction, m6), and a detail used as the opener.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpara is a text-layout lab: a fox report where tapping gaps inserts and removes paragraph breaks and the canvas re-flows with indents, a TiPToP reason pad over a highlighted story, a bat page with title and sub-heading slots plus a distractor sentence card, and a topic-sentence picker. flaginform and flagtopic sort facts by topic; none edits paragraph breaks. The 6-token shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Pupils find the rule by testing: breaking after every three sentences is rejected because sentences 3 and 4 are both about food, so the breaks land after 2 and 6 and the report shows paragraphs of 2, 4 and 2. Dropping the sentence card on a slot explains a heading has no full stop, and dropping Bats on a paragraph explains it is the title.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions on the key ideas: when to start a new paragraph (after every 3 sentences is the tempting wrong choice and the fox report disproves it) and whether a sudden new speaker needs a new paragraph (the river story then asks for the Person reason). The grouping, heading and topic-sentence steps each give a specific wrong-move message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers: three and one (paragraph length and one block), person and long (why a time jump starts a paragraph), sentence and title (sub-headings), same and headstory (new speaker), detail and off (topic sentence vs detail vs off-theme). Each message names the specific mistake and the fix.

readability.evidence: Learner audience: kid text within the 6.5 limit and adult text within 9.5 as measured by the validator. Exact Key Stage 2 terms are used: paragraph, theme, related material, heading, sub-heading, topic sentence and indent, with TiPToP named as a classroom aid rather than a curriculum term.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean and overlap under 12 percent. Every kid paragraph teaches one rule with a worked example (hedgehog themes, 2 and 4 sentences of fox facts, TiPToP, Bats and Food); adult paragraphs give the curriculum, terms, five named mistakes and what each lab step shows.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in both themes for every step: the fox report wraps to fit with a dashed tappable gap between each sentence, gap buttons wrap in rows, the four TiPToP tiles are 60 px tall, and heading cards flow onto a second row under the page. walk.cjs passes on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe finds no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark. Every canvas action has a button: three paragraph buttons, seven gap toggles with aria-pressed plus Check, four TiPToP buttons, card toggles with aria-pressed and place buttons, and topic-sentence buttons. The canvas aria-label and live text repeat every result; demos run instantly under reduced motion.
